samples.summary: Design doc still documents the removed path-matching + `@ref` tolerance, directly contradicting the paragraph right below it
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1916 still says "**Gate 1 identifies CI by workflow PATH, not by the run's display name.** … `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` and `ciConclusion()` in `checks.mjs` are the single source for both readers (`mark-ready.mjs`, `set-state.mjs`), and tolerate the `@ref` suffix a called workflow reports." That is exactly the behaviour this delta deleted (`ciRunsFor` and its `split("@")[0]`), and the very next paragraph (1918-1929) now describes it as the forgery hole (`ci.yml@pwn.yml`). The old paragraph was left in place beside its replacement, so the top-level design doc asserts both the new rule and the rule it calls exploitable. The backtick-path CI check does not catch this (no path is wrong).

samples.summary: Panel trigger comment still claims mark-ready re-derives gate 1 "from the path"
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:160-163: "mark-ready re-derives its own gate from the path (see checks.mjs CI_WORKFLOW_PATH), so promotion was never at risk". After this delta mark-ready no longer looks at any run `path`; it scopes the query with `CI_WORKFLOW_FILE` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:154). The safety argument the comment makes is still true, but the mechanism it names is gone, so the next reader auditing this trigger is pointed at a filter that no longer exists.

samples.summary: mark-ready.test.mjs comment still asserts the "exactly one CI run per head SHA" invariant this delta explicitly retracted
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:189-194 ("gate 1 reads the NEWEST CI run for the SHA"): "That is safe because a PR head SHA carries exactly one CI run … an invariant checks.test.mjs pins". The delta renamed that test to "no two ci.yml triggers can race for the same PR head SHA" and states in scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:459-465 that the old claim is FALSE (close/reopen files a second `pull_request` run). This out-of-diff comment now cites a pinned invariant that no longer exists under that name or that meaning.

samples.summary: `ciConclusion` lost its identity check: it now trusts every caller to have pre-scoped the list, with nothing at the function boundary enforcing it
samples.evidence: `ciConclusion` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:116) previously filtered to CI runs itself; it now reduces whatever array it is handed. Correctness therefore lives in two URL strings out in the callers (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:154, scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:232). The only thing preventing a future third caller from passing the unscoped `repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=` result — which would make gate 1 read `agent-review-panel`'s own green run — is a grep test hard-coded to the two file names `mark-ready.mjs` and `set-state.mjs` (scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:539). A new reader added tomorrow gets no test and no runtime guard, and the failure mode is silent promotion rather than an error. Fix belongs on the new code: have the helper (or a thin `fetchCiRuns` wrapper in checks.mjs) own the URL so the scoping cannot be forgotten.

samples.summary: New `CI_WORKFLOW_FILE` constant is duplicated as a bare `'ci.yml'` literal in three workflows, and nothing ties them to the constant
samples.evidence: agent-rerun.yml:201, agent-loop.yml:157 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:172 all pass `workflow_id: 'ci.yml'` literally (they run before checkout and cannot import checks.mjs). The delta's own test anchors on the literal too (`yml.indexOf("workflow_id: 'ci.yml'")`, scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:585) and the new test only asserts `CI_WORKFLOW_FILE === "ci.yml"`. So renaming the CI workflow file would update the constant and both JS readers while the three workflow mirrors kept querying the old name, and every existing assertion would still pass. Cheapest fix: assert the workflow literals equal `CI_WORKFLOW_FILE` in checks.test.mjs rather than a hard-coded string.
